Business Scenario: Cashier scans/taps a product with stock enabled, sufficient stock, single matching stock batch
Real-World Example: Customer puts a single 1L milk carton on the counter; cashier scans it, one shelf lot is in the system, and it drops straight into the cart with an 'Added To Cart' toast.
Current Handling: `_handleProductSelectionImpl` filters store stocks via `getStockOptionsForStore`, groups by pricing via `groupStocksByPricing`; exactly 1 group auto-selects and reserves stock via `_reserveStockForSelection`, then calls `addToCart`. Success toast `showScaffold('Added To Cart')`.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — correct fast-path behavior for the common case, no unnecessary prompts.

Business Scenario: Product has multiple stock batches at different prices/purchase costs (e.g. two purchase lots), cashier must pick which batch to sell from
Real-World Example: A bag of rice was bought in two lots — an old lot at last month's price and a new lot that cost more; cashier scans the bag and the till asks which lot this sale should draw from.
Current Handling: `groupStocksByPricing` produces >1 group; `StockSelectionModal` shown for cashier to choose. Selection then reserves stock and adds to cart.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — correct, since price/cost genuinely differs between batches and the system cannot silently pick one.

Business Scenario: Product/store has stock tracking disabled entirely (no batches recorded), cashier still needs to sell it
Real-World Example: A small shop sells loose sweets it never inventories; cashier taps the 'Sweets' tile and it rings up at the catalog price with no stock questions asked.
Current Handling: `isStockEnabled` false short-circuits all reservation logic; item added directly using base `product.price`/`mrp`, no stock deduction, no prompts.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — correct; stock-disabled products are intentionally untracked and should never block a sale.

Business Scenario: Product has zero stock rows recorded at all (never received into this store)
Real-World Example: A newly added chocolate bar was created in the catalog but no goods-received entry was ever made; cashier scans one off the shelf and it sells at the master price.
Current Handling: `getStockOptionsForStore` returns empty list; code falls back to `product.price?.price`/`product.mrp` base pricing and adds directly, no batch to reserve, no prompt.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — correct fallback; without any stock rows there is nothing to reserve against, so base pricing is the only sane behavior.

Business Scenario: Product has stock rows but every batch quantity is 0 (fully depleted, none replenished)
Real-World Example: The last case of bottled water was sold this morning so every batch reads 0, but a customer found one bottle behind the display; cashier scans it and it rings up silently at base price.
Current Handling: Same as F04 path — `getStockOptionsForStore` only returns qty>0 rows, so all-zero rows are filtered out and it falls back to base price/mrp, adds without a stock-mismatch prompt.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: Minor inconsistency: unlike the explicit out-of-stock-variant confirm (F07), a fully-depleted non-variant product sells silently with no "sell anyway" visibility to the cashier that stock is at zero. Consider surfacing the same confirm here for consistency.

Business Scenario: Stock rows exist for the product but tagged to a different store_id than the active store (e.g. central warehouse rows never adjusted for this branch)
Real-World Example: A branch cashier scans a shampoo bottle whose only stock rows belong to the central warehouse; the batch price is ignored and it sells at master price with no hint that branch stock is missing.
Current Handling: `getStockOptionsForStore` filters by `activeStore.storeId` (falls back to store-name match only if no id); mismatched rows are excluded, so item falls back to base master price instead of any batch price.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: Cashier could unknowingly sell at master price when a batch price existed for a different store — not incorrect per se (cross-store batches shouldn't apply), but there's no toast telling the cashier "no store-specific stock found, using base price," which could mask a data-sync problem.

Business Scenario: Cashier selects/taps a product variant that shows 0 recorded quantity in the system, but the physical item is in the customer's basket
Real-World Example: Customer brings a Red/L t-shirt to the counter; the system shows 0 of that size-colour in stock, but it just goes straight into the cart with the usual 'Added To Cart' toast — no stock question asked.
Entry Point: Product grid tap -> variant auto-resolve or picker
Current Handling: A "sell it anyway?" confirm exists in code (`showSellAnywayConfirmDialog` gated on `ProductVariantSelection.isOutOfStock`) but it is itself gated behind `generalSettings.confirmOversellOnZeroStock`, which is always false in practice. So the confirm path never actually triggers — an OOS variant is added silently, identical to a non-OOS one.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: Gap: the cashier gets no indication at all that the selected variant reads 0 stock — no dimming feedback survives past the picker (see F09), no toast, no confirm. If variant-level stock accuracy matters, either enable the existing confirm setting or add a lightweight non-blocking notice on add.
File Reference: lib/helpers/product_cart_helper.dart:191-216 (confirmOversellOnZeroStock gate, effectively dead); lib/features/billing/domain/product_variant_selection.dart:11 (isOutOfStock); lib/components/build_dialog_box.dart:116 (showSellAnywayConfirmDialog, unreachable in practice)

Business Scenario: Cashier scans a barcode that resolves directly to a specific out-of-stock variant (barcode encodes the variant, not just the base product)
Real-World Example: Cashier scans the tag sewn onto a Blue/M jacket; the barcode maps straight to that exact size-colour which reads 0 in stock, and it sells the same as any in-stock variant with no warning.
Current Handling: `tryResolveWithoutPicker` auto-resolves the variant from the scanned barcode (including OOS variants, by design) and hands off to `handleProductSelection`, which follows the same silent-add path as F07 (the sell-anyway confirm is unreachable).
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: Same as F07 — no signal to the cashier that the scanned variant is recorded at 0 stock.

Business Scenario: Product has multiple active variants and needs the picker sheet; one of the variants is out of stock but the others are not
Real-World Example: Customer wants a mug that comes in White, Black and Green; the picker shows all three but Green is dimmed with a red 'Out of stock' tag — the cashier can still tap Green because a customer is holding one, and it adds with no further prompt.
Entry Point: Variant picker (grid tap on multi-variant product)
Current Handling: `mobile_variant_picker_sheet.dart` (~lines 159-217) renders OOS variants at 60% opacity with a red "Out of stock" label but keeps them fully tappable; "Add to Cart" is only disabled when no variant is selected at all, not based on stock state. Selecting an OOS variant proceeds through the same silent-add path as F07 (no confirm reachable).
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None for the picker's own visual signal — dimming + label is sufficient at picker time. But once selected, the OOS signal is dropped entirely (see F07); the picker is the only place in the flow that shows stock state at all.

Business Scenario: Cashier scans a CASE/PACK/BOX barcode and there is enough base-unit stock to cover the case conversion
Real-World Example: Customer buys a full case of 24 soda cans; cashier scans the case barcode, the shop has 60 cans in stock, and one cart line for the case is added with no prompt.
Current Handling: `_findMatchingSaleUnit` matches the sale-unit barcode; conversion rate computed via `_parseSaleUnitConversionRate`; sufficient stock found in preferred sale-unit stock group, auto-selected and reserved, added without prompt.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — correct fast path when stock genuinely covers the case quantity.

Business Scenario: Cashier scans a CASE barcode but base-unit stock is short of the amount needed for that case (e.g. 1 case = 12 units, only 8 recorded)
Real-World Example: A case of 12 juice bottles is requested but only 8 loose bottles are recorded in stock; scanning the case barcode pops 'Only 8 in stock for Case (needs 12). Sell anyway?' and the cashier confirms the oversell.
Current Handling: `selectedStock.quantity < requestedQuantity` triggers `showSellAnywayConfirmDialog` with `insufficientStockConfirm` message ("Only $available in stock for $unitLabel (needs $requested). Sell anyway?"). Confirm proceeds; `addToCart`/`_reserveStockForSelection` reserves what's available and lets the rest go unreserved (oversell).
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — correct oversell-allowed behavior with explicit shortfall detail shown to the cashier, matching the fixed design intent.

Business Scenario: Cashier scans a CASE barcode for a product that has zero stock rows entirely (never tracked in this store)
Real-World Example: A wholesaler buys a case of a snack the shop has never inventoried; the cashier scans the case barcode and it drops in at base price with no warning at all, unlike the shortfall case.
Current Handling: No stock rows at all -> falls into the same base-price fallback path as F04, bypassing the insufficient-stock check entirely (there's no `selectedStock` to compare against) — sells directly with no confirm prompt at all.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: Inconsistency vs F11: a case-barcode scan with SOME insufficient stock gets a sell-anyway confirm, but a case-barcode scan with NO stock at all sells silently with zero friction. Cashier gets less warning in the more extreme shortage case. Consider triggering the same confirm (or a stronger one) when stock is entirely absent for a sale-unit scan.

Business Scenario: Cashier switches an existing cart line's unit from base (PCS) to CASE (or vice versa) via the cart unit dropdown, with sufficient or insufficient stock for the new unit
Real-World Example: Cashier rang up 6 loose water bottles then the customer says 'just give me the case'; cashier switches the cart line's unit dropdown from PCS to Case and the quantity/price re-express without being blocked.
Current Handling: `changeCartItemSaleUnit` recomputes target base quantity via conversion rate; if quantity increases it calls `_reserveStockForSelection` which allows oversell (comment explicitly notes insufficient stock never blocks a unit change); if quantity decreases, restores reservations via `_restoreStockReservations`. On provider exception, `_selectCartUnitOption` shows `showScaffoldError('Unable to change unit for this cart item.')`.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — correct; consistent with the fixed oversell-allowed design so cashiers can freely re-express quantity in a different unit without being blocked mid-sale.

Business Scenario: Cashier taps the '+' stepper on a cart line and the currently-selected stock batch still has enough quantity to cover the increment
Real-World Example: Customer decides to take a second bag of flour; cashier taps '+' on the flour line, the same lot still has plenty, and the quantity ticks to 2 instantly.
Current Handling: `syncCartItemQuantity` first tries to satisfy the increase from `getAvailableQuantityForSelection` on the current selection; if sufficient, calls `provider.setCartItemQuantity` directly with no prompts.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — correct, no interruption needed when stock is genuinely available.

Business Scenario: Cashier taps '+' and the current batch is exhausted, but an alternative batch (or several) exists for the same product
Real-World Example: Cashier bumps the quantity of cooking oil and the first lot runs out mid-increment; a second lot exists, so the till pulls from it (or asks which lot if their prices differ).
Current Handling: `getAlternativeStockOptions` (FEFO-sorted) returns candidates; `_selectAdditionalStock`/`selectionResolver` auto-picks if exactly one pricing group, otherwise shows `StockSelectionModal` for the cashier to choose.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — correct; mirrors the same single-vs-multiple-group UX used at initial add-to-cart (F01/F02).

Business Scenario: Cashier taps '+' with no alternative batch available anywhere, from a screen with a BuildContext (normal UI stepper)
Real-World Example: Customer wants a third packet of a spice but the shop's recorded stock is fully used up across all lots; tapping '+' shows 'No more stock recorded (requested 1 more). Sell anyway?' and the cashier confirms.
Current Handling: Shows `showSellAnywayConfirmDialog` ("No more stock recorded for this item (requested $remainingIncrease more). Sell anyway?"); confirm hard-sets `newQuantity` via `setCartItemQuantity`, bypassing normal reservation (oversell allowed).
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — correct; matches the fixed design intent of never hard-blocking a cashier with the item physically in hand, while still surfacing the stock discrepancy.

Business Scenario: Same as F16 but the increment is triggered programmatically/headlessly with no BuildContext available (e.g. automated sync, batch reprocessing, tests)
Real-World Example: An overnight sync job rebuilds a cart and tries to bump a line whose stock is exhausted; with no screen to ask, the operation is blocked rather than silently oversold.
Current Handling: Falls to `onBlocked('Selected stock is exhausted. No other stock is available.')` — a hard block is preserved, since there's no UI to show a confirm dialog to.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — intentional and documented tradeoff: headless callers can't present a confirm dialog, so a hard block is the only safe default there; this only affects non-interactive callers, not cashiers at the till.

Business Scenario: Cashier taps '-' on a cart line to reduce quantity, or removes the line entirely
Real-World Example: Customer changes their mind and puts back one of two yogurts; cashier taps '-' (or swipes the line away) and the reserved stock is returned to the available pool.
Current Handling: `decrementCartItem` reduces by 1 base unit (or 1 sale-unit's base equivalent) and restores the corresponding stock reservation; removes the line if quantity would drop to/below the decrement amount. `setCartItemQuantity` with newQuantity<=0 also removes the item and restores all previously deducted stock.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — correct; stock is properly returned to available pool on decrement/removal, preventing permanent stock leakage.

Business Scenario: Product is marked sellable=false (e.g. discontinued, internal-use-only item) but still exists in the catalog
Real-World Example: A cashier scans a display-only demo phone that's flagged not-for-sale; instead of adding it, the till shows 'Demo Phone is marked as not sellable' and nothing enters the cart.
Entry Point: Product grid tap, barcode scan, search+Add Item — all entry points
Current Handling: `_handleProductSelectionImpl` checks `product.sellable == false` first and calls `showScaffoldError(productNotSellable(name))` = "$name is marked as not sellable", returning before any stock/variant/price logic runs. Grid also hides such products visually.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — this is the fix: previously barcode scan could bypass the grid's visual hiding; now every entry point funnels through the same sellable check, closing that inconsistency.

Business Scenario: Cashier scans a barcode that matches no product in the local catalog at all
Real-World Example: A customer brings an imported biscuit the shop just started stocking but hasn't entered yet; scanning it opens the 'add new product with this barcode' modal so the cashier can register and sell it in one go.
Current Handling: `filteredProducts.isEmpty` opens `AddProductWithBarcodeModal(barcode: query, isAddToCart: true)` letting the cashier register a new product on the fly and add it to cart in one step.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — reasonable UX for handling genuinely new/unregistered SKUs at the till without stopping the sale.

Business Scenario: Scanned barcode encodes an embedded weight/count (prefix '000', 14 digits) but the embedded digits are malformed/non-numeric (label printer glitch, damaged barcode)
Real-World Example: A deli scale label for sliced ham is smudged so the embedded weight can't be read; the scan still adds one unit of ham instead of erroring, but no toast warns that the weight defaulted.
Current Handling: `double.tryParse`/`int.tryParse` failures set `quantity = null` instead of throwing; `handleProductSelection` defaults `quantity ?? 1`, so the item is added with quantity 1 instead of crashing or showing a false 'invalid barcode' error.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: Silent quantity substitution: cashier gets no toast indicating the embedded weight/count was unreadable and defaulted to 1 — for a weight-priced item (e.g. deli meat) this could under- or over-charge without any signal. Consider a brief warning toast when the fallback path is taken, not just a silent default.

Business Scenario: Product's resolved unit price is zero (no price configured, or price data pending) but cashier needs to sell it now
Real-World Example: A freshly imported grocery item still has price 0 because pricing hasn't synced; scanning it pops a quick price/qty entry box, and if the cashier cancels they see 'Price not entered — item was not added to cart'.
Current Handling: `ZeroPriceQuickEntryHelper.isZeroPrice` triggers a quick price/qty entry modal (`promptForProduct`) before adding; cancel now shows `showScaffoldError(zeroPriceEntryCancelled)` = "Price not entered — item was not added to cart" instead of silently doing nothing.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — this is the fix; the cashier now gets explicit feedback that the item was NOT added, preventing a customer from walking out with an unrung item nobody notices.

Business Scenario: Customer's purchase-history price (used to auto-suggest a price based on prior purchases) would fall below the configured minimum margin/price floor for the product
Real-World Example: A regular wholesale customer last bought sugar at a special low rate; the till tries to auto-apply that old price but it now sits below the store's minimum margin, so it is rejected and clamped up to the floor.
Entry Point: Customer purchase-history price auto-apply (cart price field)
Current Handling: `applyPurchaseHistoryPrice` computes `minimumSalePriceForProduct` (based on min margin % and/or min margin price, whichever floor is more restrictive) and rejects the historical price (applied:false, belowMinimumPrice set) if it's under that floor; `commitDisplayPrice` also clamps any manually-typed price up to the floor.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: Gap (variant-blind): `minimumSalePriceForProduct` computes the floor purely from the base product's price/margin fields and never consults `variant.price`/`variant.effectivePrice`. A variant intentionally priced below the base product's margin (e.g. a clearance colorway with its own lower price) has any purchase-history or manually-typed price on that variant's cart line clamped up to the BASE product's floor, not the variant's own — silently overriding a legitimate lower variant price.

Business Scenario: Cashier re-scans/re-adds a product that's already on the cart with a manually-overridden price (e.g. negotiated discount) — does the override survive or get overwritten by catalog price?
Real-World Example: Cashier negotiated a lower price on a floor fan and typed it in; the customer wants a second fan, so re-scanning it bumps the quantity to 2 while keeping the agreed price instead of snapping back to catalog price.
Entry Point: Barcode scan / grid tap on a product already in cart
Current Handling: `handleProductSelection` detects a matching existing cart line (by productId+saleUnitId+variantId+stockGroupIds) and passes `priceToUse = null`, deferring to `addToCart`'s existing-item branch which only overwrites `price`/`mrp` when the incoming value is non-null and `isManualPriceOverride` isn't set — so the manual override is preserved, just the quantity increments.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — correct; a cashier's negotiated/manual price isn't silently clobbered by a re-scan, while quantity still increases as expected.

Business Scenario: addToCart (or a related lookup) is invoked with a productId that doesn't exist locally yet — e.g. product record hasn't finished syncing down from server
Real-World Example: A held order references a product that hasn't finished downloading to this device yet; restoring the cart looks it up, gets a safe null instead of crashing the app.
Entry Point: Barcode scan, programmatic re-add, sync-triggered cart rebuild
Current Handling: `getProductById` uses `_products.firstWhere(...)` wrapped so a not-found case returns `null` rather than throwing; callers that previously used unguarded `firstWhere` (which threw an uncaught exception) are now null-safe.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — this is the fix; removes a crash vector when the local product cache is momentarily behind the cart/order data (common in an offline-first sync model).

Business Scenario: Cashier opens the multi-batch stock-selection modal (>1 pricing group) then dismisses it by tapping outside or hitting cancel, without picking a batch
Real-World Example: Cashier scans a rice bag with two price lots, the batch chooser opens, but they fat-finger outside it to close it; now they see 'No batch selected — item was not added to cart' rather than assuming it rang up.
Entry Point: Stock selection modal (shown from F02/F15 flows)
Current Handling: `result == null` from the modal now triggers `showScaffoldError(stockNotSelected)` = "No batch selected — item was not added to cart" instead of silently doing nothing.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — this is the fix; previously an accidental outside-tap silently dropped the add with zero feedback, which could mean a cashier believes an item is rung up when it isn't.

Business Scenario: Product has multiple stock batches at the SAME price but different expiry/received dates; repeated adds of the same product should deplete oldest stock first
Real-World Example: Two lots of yogurt sit at the same price but different expiry dates; as the cashier rings up several cups, the system draws from the batch expiring first to avoid spoilage write-offs.
Entry Point: Repeated barcode scans / stepper increments of the same product
Current Handling: `_sortStocksForReservation` sorts candidate stocks by `expiryDate` ascending, then `date` (received) ascending, then `id` ascending (FEFO), and `_reserveStockForSelection` deducts across candidates in that order; `getAlternativeStockOptions` and the modal's `CombinedStock.firstStock` use the same ordering for display.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — correct FEFO behavior, minimizing spoilage/expiry write-offs, and consistently applied both for deduction and for what metadata is shown to the cashier.

Business Scenario: Multiple stock batches share identical pricing-relevant fields (price, unit, tax rate, etc.) — should they collapse into a single cart line, or does each distinct-priced batch need its own line?
Real-World Example: Three deliveries of the same biscuit all landed at the identical price and tax; when the cashier sells it, the cart shows one clean 'Biscuit x3' line instead of three confusing duplicate lines.
Current Handling: `groupStocksByPricing` builds a grouping key from `kDefaultStockGroupingFields` (price, unit) plus other active fields (mrp, purchasePrice, hsnCode, taxRate, wholesalePrice, wholesaleMinUnit) via `buildStockGroupingKey`; batches sharing the same key collapse into one `CombinedStock`/cart line, while genuinely different pricing produces separate groups (and thus the F02 modal).
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — correct; avoids splitting a sale across visually-identical-priced batches into confusing duplicate cart lines, while still separating genuinely different price tiers.

Business Scenario: Cashier increases quantity on a cart line past the wholesale minimum-unit threshold (e.g. buying 12+ units triggers a case/wholesale price)
Real-World Example: A shopkeeper buying for resale bumps soap bars from 10 to 12; crossing the 12-unit wholesale threshold, the line price automatically drops to the wholesale rate with no manual discount needed.
Current Handling: `setCartItemQuantity` recomputes wholesale eligibility on every quantity change via `_qualifiesForWholesalePrice` (quantity >= wholesaleMinUnit AND wholesalePrice configured), and `_resolveUnitPrice`'s fallback chain applies wholesale price as second priority (after sale-unit price, before retail/base price) when eligible.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — correct automatic re-pricing; cashier doesn't need to manually swap units or apply a manual discount to get the wholesale rate once the threshold is crossed. Note: for a variant line, variant price takes precedence over wholesale price in `_resolveUnitPrice`'s fallback chain (see F46 addendum) — wholesale re-pricing on quantity crossing only applies when no variant price is in play.

Business Scenario: Cashier attempts to save/confirm/checkout an order or quotation while the cart is empty
Real-World Example: A distracted cashier taps 'Save Order' before scanning anything; the till refuses with 'Add items to cart' rather than creating a blank order.
Entry Point: Save order / confirm order / save quotation buttons
Current Handling: Multiple explicit empty-cart guards throughout `billing_page.dart` check `cartItems.isEmpty` before each checkout-adjacent action and show a contextual `showScaffoldError` (e.g. 'billing.add_items_to_cart'.tr for save order, 'Please add items to quote first.' for quotation).
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — correct and consistently guarded across all the relevant checkout entry points found (save order, confirm, save quotation).

Business Scenario: Cashier scans the same barcode twice in very quick succession (double-scan from a fast trigger-happy scanner, or a queued duplicate)
Real-World Example: A jumpy scanner fires twice on one pass of a shampoo bottle; the two scans are queued and processed one after another, so the second correctly sees the stock the first already took rather than racing it.
Current Handling: Barcodes are serialized through `_enqueueBarcode`/`_processNextBarcode`, processing one at a time via `_processBarcodeInternal`; each call goes through the full stock-reservation path sequentially, so a second scan sees the already-decremented stock from the first and reserves/oversells accordingly rather than racing on stale data.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None apparent from the queueing design — sequential processing avoids a race condition on stock deduction; would need a live device test to confirm no queue item can be dropped, but the code structure protects against concurrent double-deduction.

Business Scenario: Store has no internet connectivity — does any part of the add-to-cart/quantity-change flow get blocked because of it (it shouldn't, since this is an offline-first POS)
Real-World Example: The shop's broadband is down during a storm but customers keep queuing; the cashier keeps scanning, adjusting quantities and building carts normally, with only the final online 'confirm order' step held back.
Current Handling: No connectivity/`isOnline` gating was found wrapping `addToCart`, `setCartItemQuantity`, `changeCartItemSaleUnit`, or any of the stock-reservation helpers. Connectivity gating is confined to online-only actions (confirm/create-order network calls) via `BillingMobileConnectivityController.canConfirmOnline`/`shouldBlockOnlineCheckout`, using distinct messages (`noInternetConfirm`, `noInternetCreateOrder`).
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — correct; cart building and stock reservation remain fully local/offline-capable as required for a POS, with connectivity checks scoped only to genuinely server-dependent actions.

Business Scenario: Cashier applies a discount or coupon to the cart when the cart is empty, or enters a negative/oversized discount value
Real-World Example: A cashier types a 150% discount or a flat discount bigger than the bill total by mistake; the till rejects it with a clear message instead of producing a negative-total sale.
Current Handling: Explicit validation messages exist: `emptyCartDiscount`, `discountNegative`, `discountPercentMax`, `discountFlatExceedsTotal`, `applyCouponFailed`, `couponInvalid(name)` — each guards its respective bad-input case before applying.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None apparent from the message set — validation appears comprehensive for the common bad-input cases (empty cart, negative, over-100%, flat discount exceeding total, invalid coupon code).

Business Scenario: Cart line quantity or price changes, and inclusive tax must be recalculated for the line (tax-inclusive pricing model)
Real-World Example: A customer buys 3 instead of 1 of a tax-inclusive drink; as the quantity changes the VAT portion of the line recomputes on the spot so the tax breakdown on the bill stays correct.
Entry Point: Cart quantity +/- stepper, price override entry
Current Handling: `inclusiveTaxAmount` recomputes as `(unitPrice * qty * rate) / (100 + rate)` on demand whenever quantity or price changes, and `addToCart`'s new-item branch resolves tax rate/amount via `_resolveCartTaxRate`/`_calculateTaxAmount` at insertion time.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — correct; tax recalculates live off current unit price and quantity rather than being cached/stale after a quantity or price edit.

Business Scenario: [RESOLVED] Cart add-to-cart previously could be invoked via an older `handleAddProductToCart` helper (a separate/legacy entry point) rather than through `ProductCartHelper`
Real-World Example: This used to be like having two different cash registers in the shop that rang up sales slightly differently — one had all the safety checks (like the not-sellable warning), the other didn't. That second, unsafe register has since been unplugged and removed entirely, so every sale now goes through the one till with all the checks.
Entry Point: N/A (was: any screen still wired to the legacy stock_selection_helper entry point)
Current Handling: `lib/helpers/stock_selection_helper.dart` no longer exists anywhere in `lib/` — confirmed by direct file search. The dead-code risk this row previously flagged has been eliminated by deletion.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — resolved. Row kept as a record that this cleanup was completed; no further action needed.

Business Scenario: Cashier scans a barcode that maps directly to a specific variant that HAS its own scoped stock rows (variant-labelled stock received into this store)
Real-World Example: Cashier scans the tag on a Green/S hoodie that was received as its own labelled stock; the sale draws from that Green/S batch's price and quantity, not a shared hoodie pool, and the picker's cached count drops accordingly.
Current Handling: `tryResolveWithoutPicker` matches the variant by barcode; `ProductCartHelper` then draws stock via `LocalProductProvider.filterStocksForVariant(...)` which keeps only rows whose `Stock.productVariantId == variantId`, so pricing/reservation come from that variant's own batches, and `_reserveStockForSelection`/`_adjustVariantQuantity` deducts both the scoped stock row and the cached `ProductVariant.quantity`.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — correct variant-scoped draw-down; the sale deducts from the right variant's stock rather than a shared pool, and the picker's cached variant quantity stays in step.

Business Scenario: Cashier sells a variant that has NO variant-scoped stock rows recorded — only general (non-variant) stock exists for the product
Real-World Example: A store enabled variants for a t-shirt but only ever received it as generic (untagged) stock; selling a Red/M unit quietly draws from that general pool with no signal that per-variant tracking is missing.
Entry Point: Variant picker / variant barcode / single-variant auto-resolve
Current Handling: `filterStocksForVariant` finds no rows with a matching `productVariantId`, so it falls back to rows where `productVariantId == null` (general product stock) and draws pricing/reservation from those instead of returning empty.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: Acceptable fallback, but it is silent: a store that intends per-variant stock tracking but has un-tagged (variantId null) rows will quietly sell against general stock with no signal that variant-level tracking is missing for that SKU. Consider surfacing when a scoped-variant sale falls back to general stock so mis-tagged inventory is noticed.

Business Scenario: Product has exactly one active variant (single-variant SKU) and cashier taps it from the grid without scanning a variant barcode
Real-World Example: A perfume comes in just one 'Standard 50ml' variant; tapping its grid tile skips the picker entirely and adds it straight to the cart while still stamping the cart line with the variant id.
Current Handling: `tryResolveWithoutPicker` returns `active.first` when `activeVariants.length == 1`, so no picker sheet is shown; the lone variant is auto-selected and its price/mrp resolve via `effectivePrice`/`resolveVariantMrp` before add-to-cart.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — correct; a single-variant product should not force an extra picker tap, while the cart line still carries the variant id/attributes for downstream order payload and stock scoping.

Business Scenario: Store has the PRODUCT_VARIANT_ENABLED setting turned OFF, but catalog products still carry variant data from the server
Real-World Example: A store that doesn't want variant complexity turns the feature off; tapping a t-shirt that still carries size/colour data adds it as a plain product at base price, with no picker and no variant stamped. (Note: a product whose variants are ALL inactive with the flag ON also correctly falls through to plain-product add — no empty picker.)
Entry Point: Product grid tap, barcode scan (mobile add flow)
Current Handling: `addProductWithVariantResolution` reads `productVariantEnabled` from `AppSettingsProvider`; when false it skips `tryResolveWithoutPicker`/`needsVariantPicker` entirely (`selectedVariant` stays null) and the product is added as a plain product using base price/mrp. Setting defaults to true when the flag is absent from server settings. Verified: when the flag is ON but `activeVariants` is empty, `tryResolveWithoutPicker` returns null and `needsVariantPicker` is false, so no empty picker is shown.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: Behavior is correct for the gate, but partial: only the mobile add path (`add_product_with_variant.dart`) and the create/edit variant editors honor the flag. Stock scoping (`filterStocksForVariant`) still keys off `Stock.productVariantId` regardless of the flag — harmless when no variant is selected, but the gate is enforced at the orchestration layer only, not globally.

Business Scenario: A variant line is sold (order confirmed) then later returned via sales return — the picker's cached per-variant quantity must fall then rise back
Real-World Example: A customer returns a Blue/L shirt they bought yesterday; the local cached Blue/L count that drives the picker's out-of-stock dimming ticks back up, mirroring the reservation drop that happened at sale time.
Current Handling: On reservation `_adjustVariantQuantity(productId, variantId, -reserved)` decrements the cached `ProductVariant.quantity`; on return `_adjustVariantQuantity(..., restored)` adds it back, with `copyWith(quantity: clamped)` preventing the cached count from going negative.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None for the cached count itself — it is clamped and symmetric. Caveat: this only keeps the LOCAL cached `ProductVariant.quantity` (used by the picker's OOS dimming) in step; authoritative variant stock still comes from the server sync, so the cached value is a best-effort UI mirror, not a source of truth.

Business Scenario: Staff opens an already-placed order's details and a line item was sold as a specific variant
Real-World Example: A manager reviews yesterday's invoice and one line was a White/XL polo; the order details screen shows 'White | XL' under the product name so they know exactly which variant was sold.
Current Handling: `OrderDetailsModelDataCartItem` parses `product_variant_id` and `variant_attributes` (Map or JSON-string, via `_parseVariantAttributes`) and exposes `formattedVariantAttributes` (values joined with ' | '); the order details widget renders that line under the product name when non-empty.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None for on-screen display. Gap: the receipt/print pipeline is a separate receipt-params path and was deliberately NOT updated, so a printed/thermal receipt still shows the base product name with no variant attribute line even though the on-screen order details do.

Business Scenario: Staff opens a sales return and a returned line was originally sold as a specific variant
Real-World Example: Processing a return of a Black/38 pair of jeans, the sales-return screen shows 'Black | 38' beneath the item name so the clerk confirms the returned item matches what was sold.
Current Handling: `ListSalesReturnItems` parses `product_variant_id`/`variant_attributes` and exposes `formattedVariantAttributes`; `sales_return.dart` renders the attribute line beneath the item name when non-empty, so returns are attributed to the correct variant visually.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None on-screen. Same receipt caveat as F41 applies if a return slip is printed via the receipt-params pipeline.

Business Scenario: Admin creates a NEW product and defines one or more variants (size/colour rows) in the create modal
Real-World Example: A shop owner adds a new t-shirt and enters four rows — Red/S, Red/M, Blue/S, Blue/M — each with its own barcode and price; validation blocks duplicate attribute sets or barcodes before saving.
Current Handling: Variant editor rows are converted to `VariantFormInput` and passed to `buildCreateVariantsPayload`, which drops deletion-flagged rows and emits `{sku, barcode, price, mrp, purchase_price, active:true, attributes:[{product_prop_id, value}]}` per PRODUCT_VARIANTS_API.md §1; `validateVariantRows` enforces at-least-one-attribute, unique attribute sets, unique barcodes, and numeric >=0 prices before submit. Whole section is gated by `productVariantEnabled`.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None in the pure payload builder (unit-tested). Depends on `list-product-properties` for the attribute dropdown (see F45), whose response shape is defensively guessed; if the real API returns a different shape the property options could come back empty and force manual attribute entry.

Business Scenario: Admin edits an existing product's variants — modifying some, adding new ones, and removing others
Real-World Example: An owner discontinues the Green colourway of a mug, adds a new Yellow one, and bumps the price on White; the edit payload sends deletes, creates and updates together in one save.
Current Handling: `buildEditVariantsPayload` (PRODUCT_VARIANTS_API.md §2) maps rows with an `id` to updates, rows without an id to creates, and deletion-flagged rows with an id to `{id, _delete:true}`; deletion-flagged rows that were never persisted (no id) are dropped. Attributes are always sent as the complete set because the server replaces them wholesale.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None in the builder logic. Correctness of the `_delete` and wholesale-attribute-replacement semantics rests on PRODUCT_VARIANTS_API.md being an accurate description of the server contract; not verifiable from the client alone.

Business Scenario: Variant editor needs the list of attribute properties (e.g. COLOR, SIZE and their allowed values) to populate the attribute dropdowns
Real-World Example: When the owner opens the variant editor, the COLOR and SIZE dropdowns should be pre-filled from the server; if that fetch returns an unexpected shape they silently come back empty and the owner is left typing attributes by hand.
Entry Point: Add product modal / edit dialog open
Current Handling: `fetchProductProperties` calls `GET /api/v1/product/list-product-properties` and caches results on `ProductProvider`; failures are caught and logged (`debugPrint('⚠️ fetchProductProperties failed')`) rather than blocking the modal.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: Real risk: the `ProductProperty` model documents that the response shape is NOT fixed and is parsed defensively (guessed). If the live endpoint returns a shape the parser doesn't anticipate, properties silently come back empty and the editor degrades to free-text/manual attribute entry with no error surfaced to the admin. Needs validation against the real API response.

Business Scenario: A selected variant has its own price/mrp override vs a variant that only carries attributes and inherits the base product price
Real-World Example: One shirt colour is on promotion with its own lower price while the other colours just inherit the standard shirt price; selling either draws the right price automatically, and a cashier's typed override still beats both.
Current Handling: Price resolves via `ProductVariantSelection.resolveVariantPrice` -> `variant.effectivePrice(productPrice)` (variant price when set, else base product price); mrp via `resolveVariantMrp` (variant.mrp when >0, else product mrp, else effective price). `ProductCartHelper` re-applies the same resolution unless the cashier typed an explicit price override.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: Gap (ordering inconsistency, not covered by original row): at add-to-cart time the initial price is computed purely from the variant (`product_cart_helper.dart:232-240`), with no reference to any selected sale unit. But on any later refresh (`_refreshCartItemPricing` -> `_resolveUnitPrice`, `local_product_provider.dart:672-716`), the precedence is sale-unit price FIRST, then variant price, then wholesale, then retail. So a cart line for a variant that also carries a sale-unit (case/pack) selection can silently re-price from the variant rate to the sale-unit rate on a later quantity change or forced refresh, with no toast shown. Otherwise the base inheritance chain (variant override vs base price vs manual override) remains correct as originally documented.
File Reference: lib/features/billing/domain/product_variant_selection.dart:86-110; lib/helpers/product_cart_helper.dart:232-240 (variant-only price at add); lib/providers/local_product_provider.dart:672-716 (_resolveUnitPrice, sale-unit-before-variant precedence at refresh)

Business Scenario: A variant sale is completed and a receipt is printed / re-printed for the customer
Real-World Example: A customer who bought a 'T-Shirt (Red | L)' gets a printed receipt that just says 'T-Shirt' with no size or colour, making a later exchange harder to match to the slip.
Current Handling: Order-details and sales-return MODELS and their on-screen UIs render the variant attribute line (F41/F42), but the receipt/print templates were intentionally left on the separate receipt-params pipeline and not updated for variants.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: Known gap: a printed receipt shows only the base product name, so a customer buying "T-Shirt (Red | L)" gets a slip that reads "T-Shirt" with no size/colour, making exchanges/returns harder to reconcile against the physical item. Updating the receipt-params pipeline to include variant attributes is outstanding follow-up work.

Business Scenario: Cashier opens the multi-batch stock selection modal (F02) for a variant that has several variant-scoped batches at different prices
Real-World Example: A Blue/M shirt was received in two price lots; when the cashier sells one the batch chooser lists both lots, but the rows show only price/date with no 'Blue/M' label to confirm they're looking at the right variant's batches.
Current Handling: `filterStocksForVariant` narrows the candidate stocks to the chosen variant before `groupStocksByPricing` builds the modal groups, so the batches shown genuinely belong to that variant; selection then reserves against those scoped rows. Confirmed: `filterStocksForVariant` is an either/or fallback (variant-scoped rows exclusively, or all unscoped rows if none exist) — not a union — so there is no double-counting risk between F37's general-stock fallback and this modal.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: Gap: the `StockSelectionModal` rows are labelled by pricing/batch fields only and are NOT tagged as belonging to a specific variant in the UI. When general-stock fallback (F37) mixes in, or when a cashier is verifying they picked the right variant's batch, there's no variant label in the modal to confirm scope. Consider surfacing the variant attributes in the modal header/rows.

Business Scenario: An open cart line, or a held/saved order, references a product variant that gets deactivated or deleted server-side after the line was added
Real-World Example: A cashier adds a Green/M hoodie to a held order at its variant price; before the order is confirmed, an admin discontinues (deactivates) that variant from the back office. Reopening the held order and bumping the quantity keeps the line at its original Green/M price — the deactivation elsewhere doesn't touch it.
Entry Point: Held/saved order reopen, or any quantity/price refresh on an existing cart line
Current Handling: VERIFIED BY TEST (test/variant_deactivated_pricing_test.dart) — corrected from an earlier static-analysis-only finding. `_refreshCartItemPricing` (`local_product_provider.dart:718-733`) always resolves pricing from `item.product`, the product/variant snapshot frozen onto the `LocalCartItem` at add-to-cart time — it never re-reads the live `_products` catalog. So a variant deactivated after being added does NOT affect the already-added line's price on a later quantity change; the line keeps selling at its original variant price.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: None — this is correct/safe behavior, not a gap. (Earlier version of this row incorrectly claimed the price silently falls back to base/wholesale; dynamic testing disproved that — the frozen snapshot means it doesn't.) Note this only concerns an EXISTING cart line; a brand-new add of that same (now-inactive) variant is separately prevented since `activeVariants` filtering keeps deactivated variants out of the picker/auto-resolve for new adds.

Business Scenario: Master data / admin config changes the active stock-grouping fields (e.g. toggling whether purchase price or HSN code participates in grouping) while a cashier already has an open cart
Real-World Example: A cashier already rang up 2 tins of paint from the same batch on one cart line; mid-shift, an admin changes a background pricing setting from head office. When the cashier scans a 3rd tin from that same batch, it shows up as a brand-new second line instead of bumping the existing line to 3 — the bill total is still correct, it just looks like two separate entries for the same paint.
Entry Point: Barcode scan / grid tap while cart is non-empty, config changes mid-session
Current Handling: `setActiveStockGroupingFields` is re-applied from `masterDataProvider.activeStockGroupingFields` on every `_handleProductSelectionImpl` call, so a new add uses whatever fields are current NOW; `_findCartItemIndex`'s grouped-line match compares pricing signatures via `_stockGroupingKeyForStock`, which is computed fresh each time from the CURRENT active fields for both the incoming and the existing item's stock. If the field set changed between the two adds, the two signatures can differ even though the underlying batch is identical, so the items end up on separate lines instead of collapsing.
Disadvantage / Improvement Needed: Gap: not tested/documented anywhere in this analysis (closest is F28, which assumes a static grouping config for the whole session). A live config change mid-cart is a rare but real scenario in a multi-device/admin-managed setup; splitting an otherwise-identical batch across two cart lines is a minor confusion but not a correctness bug (totals still sum correctly).
